facts.text: HopperURDFEnvV3 subclasses gym.Env
HopperURDFEnv-v3 is registered with entry point my_pybullet_envs:HopperURDFEnvV3 and max_episode_steps=500
The physics timestep is 1/500 s per Bullet substep
An environment step advances the simulation for range(control_skip) physics substeps and increments the timer at each substep
control_skip has constructor default 10
The action space is Box(low=-1, high=+1) with one element per controlled joint
The robot has three controlled joints, ctrl_dofs [3, 4, 5]
The action is compressed with tanh before it is used as the joint command
apply_action scales the action by max_forces and writes it as the torque of the controlled joints
max_forces starts as nominal_max_forces, [200.0] * 3
The observation is the five joint positions a_q[1:] followed by the six joint velocities a_dq
obs_scaling is [1.0] * 5 + [1.0] * 2 + [0.1] * 4: the last four velocities are scaled by 0.1
The observation space is Box(-inf, +inf) with one bound per observation value
The episode is not done only while every controlled joint speed is below 50 and the height is between 0.6 and 1.8
step returns (observation, reward, not not_done, {'sas_window': ...})
The reward is a 3.0 alive bonus, plus the average forward speed, minus 0.5 times the squared action sum, minus 3.0 per joint at its limit and minus an acceleration penalty capped at 5.0
The acceleration penalty weight acc_pen_weight defaults to 0.05
reset restarts the simulation, applies the timestep _ts and sets gravity (0, 0, -10)
The robot starts at base_init_pos [0, 0, 1.3] with zero orientation
With init_noise the reset perturbs the initial joint positions by 0.02 and velocities by 0.1
reset() takes no seed argument
seed(seed) replaces np_random with gym.utils.seeding.np_random(seed)
render defaults to True and opens a PyBullet GUI connection; render=False uses a headless client
The constructor selects the soft-floor, deformable-floor, low-power, EMF-power, heavy-head and randomization variants with boolean options
The model loads assets/hopper_my.urdf, or assets/hopper_my_heavyhead.urdf when heavy_head is set
The README creates a Python 3.6 conda environment and installs requirements.txt

determinism.notes: cap.world.seed.v1 or a reset seed fixes the reset perturbation of the fake and the update is deterministic, so one fake repeats a trajectory for the same seed and actions; the upstream uses numpy's generator and adds observation and action noise by default, so the two do not share trajectories

gaps: the fake backend is a kinematic stand-in: no rigid-body, contact, actuator, sensor or noise model and no PyBullet, so it is F0 and cannot reproduce the upstream contact dynamics

the upstream advances physics at 1/500 s and applies the action for a constructor-default control_skip=10 substeps (a 20 ms control period by default); the fake advances one 20 ms transition from a made-up kinematic update

the fake draws the reset perturbation from Python's random.Random while upstream uses numpy's generator, and the upstream adds observation and action noise by default, so a seed gives different trajectories on the two
the upstream termination and reward terms are computed here against the fake's kinematic state; the fake does not reproduce the upstream joint torques, forward speed or joint-limit penalties
no rendering and no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by timestep_ms only; the upstream constructor opens a PyBullet GUI unless render=False
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state/set_state
the upstream environment class never truncates; the registration max_episode_steps=500 is applied by gym.make, not by this fake and not by the bridge, so the fake has no truncation flag

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the fake state is kept and stays readable
